annotation.title_clean: The urgency of robot trading regulation in Indonesia: Between innovation and investor protection
annotation.title_en: The urgency of robot trading regulation in Indonesia: Between innovation and investor protection
annotation.venue: International Journal of Civil Law and Legal Research
annotation.summary_en: Normative legal study arguing Indonesia needs specific regulation of software 'robot trading' (automated trading systems) to protect investors and market stability, citing fragmented OJK/Bappebti oversight and Ponzi-style fraud. It proposes a balanced framework of definition, tiered licensing, algorithm standards, disclosures, sandboxes and enforcement.
key_provisions_or_claims: Indonesia lacks specific regulation for robot trading; existing rules are general.
Regulatory fragmentation between OJK and Bappebti creates exploitable gaps.
Recommends a clear legal definition and tiered licensing and registration.
Calls for algorithm testing standards, risk disclosures, and truth-in-advertising rules.
Proposes regulatory sandboxes, investor education, international cooperation and strong sanctions.
